name: Ibn Abdun
bio: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Majid ibn Abdun, called “holder of the two vizierates”, was one of the leading men of letters of al-Andalus in his day; he was born in Evora (Yabura), in present-day Portugal, and died there. He served as vizier to the Aftasid kings of Badajoz until their fall, and afterwards worked for the Almoravids who had overthrown them. He was a master of the formal epistle and learned in history and hadith, and al-Zirikli records that he knew the Book of Songs by heart. His best-known poem is al-Bassama, his elegy for the Aftasids, which Ibn Badrun and others wrote commentaries on. He died in 529 AH (1135 CE), though other dates are given.
